clue.text: Money teachers make from this confection?

parts.note: dough is slang for money
the NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A question of what cash teachers might raise by selling cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut is a fried sweet cake, a kind of confection.

clue.text: Carefree girl coming out — and where she's walking?

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a girl making her debut in society
someone overjoyed is said to be walking on air

explanation.surface: A debutante, free of care, floats along at her coming-out.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, cheerful and untroubled manner.

clue.text: Garments submerged in a northern river

parts.note: something submerged is under the water
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: Clothes are found sunk in a river in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in County Durham, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes are garments worn beneath other clothing.

clue.text: Fruity sound from front part of ship

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word heard the same as the fruit word

parts.note: haws are the red fruits of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: A fruit-like noise comes from the bow of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawse is the part of a ship's bow through which the anchor cables pass.

clue.text: One who in Paris, and in Marseilles, is perturbed

parts.note: un is French for one
qui is French for who
et is French for and

explanation.surface: Somebody in two French cities is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' and 'in Marseilles' tell you that each word before them is to be put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Unquiet means restless or uneasy, a state of being agitated.

clue.text: Preoccupy ex-pupils with. 27's conclusion

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school
27 across is AUTHORESS, whose closing three letters are ESS

explanation.surface: Former pupils are kept busy with the ending of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'with' is a print slip; read 'with 27's conclusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to fill someone's mind continually, to engross them.

clue.text: Such a lie, so to describe Dr Grace!

definitions.text: Such a lie, so to describe Dr Grace!

parts.words: Such a lie, so to describe Dr Grace!
parts.note: a shameless lie has a stock adjective; applied literally to W.G. Grace it would mean beardless, which he famously was not

explanation.surface: A shameless untruth, and an absurd way to describe the famously bearded cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr W.G. Grace, the Victorian cricketer, had a huge beard, so calling him clean-shaven would itself be a brazen falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazen or shameless lie is a barefaced one; literally the word means having no beard.

clue.text: Letter satisfied an old busybody

parts.note: em is the name of the letter M
met as in met a demand, satisfied it

explanation.surface: A letter satisfied an elderly meddler.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'busybody' is the busy ant, not a meddler.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is an old dialect word for an ant, the proverbially busy insect.

clue.text: A record for being celibate

explanation.surface: A disc for someone who stays unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: A single is a short record release; single also means unmarried, living alone.

clue.text: Standard lines about a woman

indicators.note: the railway abbreviation goes around the woman's name

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway lines
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Normal railway lines are found around a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag carried on a pole, as is a banner.

clue.text: Garden plot we return to sprinkle

parts.note: a bed is a plot for growing flowers

indicators.note: the word we is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: Gardeners come back to water a flower patch.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedew is to wet with drops, as dew does.

clue.text: Blaster in the capacity of BR employee? About right

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: the railway worker goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a ry man, a railway man, worked for British Rail; RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone working as a railwayman turns out to be a demolition expert.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is the standard abbreviation for railway, so a railway man is RY MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarryman uses explosives to blast rock out of a quarry.

clue.text: Extremely opaque warning shaking Ibsen, for one

indicators.note: the letters are shaken up into a new order
the very ends of the word opaque are taken

explanation.surface: An unclear caution unsettles the playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives OE, the first and last letters of opaque; 'shaking' rearranges OE with WARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the playwright, was a native of Norway.

clue.text: It's disastrous for a corpulent man

parts.note: corpulent means fat
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A warning that obesity can kill a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly or ruinous events are disastrous in the extreme.

clue.text: Arctic feature of one church measure

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England
a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Something in the far north belongs to a church measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefoot is a belt of ice fixed along a polar shoreline.

clue.text: Go too far and jeer after the cricket

indicators.note: the jeering word comes after the cricket term

parts.note: overs are the units of play in cricket, six balls each
to hoot is to jeer

explanation.surface: Booing follows the cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to pass beyond a target, to exceed it.

clue.text: Fictitious bird, with ducks round about, in Watteau's style

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird

indicators.note: the two ducks go round the abbreviation

parts.note: a duck is a nought, O, in cricket; two give OO
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A mythical bird with ducks around it, as painted by Watteau.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Watteau painted in the ornate eighteenth-century rococo manner.

clue.text: The drink for Bluntschli?

parts.note: Bluntschli is Shaw's soldier in Arms and the Man who carries sweets instead of bullets, nicknamed after a cream confection

explanation.surface: What would a certain Swiss soldier like to drink?
explanation.walkthrough: In Shaw's Arms and the Man, Bluntschli is the 'chocolate cream soldier'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluntschli prefers sweets to cartridges, so a cocoa drink suits him.

clue.text: Compete with Portland — a stuck-up advertiser, maybe

parts.note: to play is to compete
Portland Bill is a headland on the Dorset coast

explanation.surface: Competing with a snobbish advertiser from Portland.
explanation.walkthrough: Portland Bill is a well-known headland in Dorset, England. 'Stuck-up' means snooty in the surface but pasted up on a wall in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a poster pasted up to advertise a show.

clue.text: Eager to have paintings, say, around the study

indicators.note: the painting word goes round the room word

parts.note: paintings are an example of art
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Keen to hang pictures around the study.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, keen and enthusiastic.

clue.text: Column in unfinished state for a scoop

indicators.note: the column word goes inside the shortened verb
the last letter of the verb is dropped

parts.note: to state is to tell
a row is a line, like a column

explanation.surface: A column goes into an incomplete statement about a scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests a newspaper column beside the 'scoop', but here it is a row; 'unfinished' trims the verb, and 'in' places the row inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool with a scooping blade.

clue.text: Leftist voting for one of the herd

parts.note: a red is a left-wing person
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A left-winger votes to join the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Poll is a hornless British breed of cattle.

clue.text: Non-acceptance of upper-class student — safer, perhaps?

indicators.note: the letters may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: U means upper-class
L is a learner

explanation.surface: Rejecting a posh student as a safer option.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a rejection of an offer.

clue.text: Not enough butter? What predicament

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at a tiny smear of butter on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a thin layer of spread; it is also an awkward fix or difficulty.

clue.text: Suit in evidence in St James's

explanation.surface: A suit worn in the posh part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: St James's is the London district famous for gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is a suit of playing cards; St James's in London is full of private members' clubs.

clue.text: Goethe's mother lost her head, being unqualified

indicators.note: the first letter of the German word is removed

parts.note: Mutter is German for mother, Goethe being German

explanation.surface: The German poet's mother was beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means complete, absolute, without qualification.

clue.text: Present minister perhaps has this handed to him on a plate

definitions.text: this handed to him on a plate

parts.note: to present is to offer
a government minister may be a Tory, a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A clergyman is given the church collection on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'minister' looks like a clergyman, which fits the definition, but in the wordplay it is a Tory politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The collection taken during a church service is passed to the priest on a plate.

clue.text: River horse, some call it

indicators.note: spoken, the horse word is heard like the river

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed coat

explanation.surface: Some people call a horse by the name of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major European waterway through Switzerland and France.

clue.text: George Eliot, for one, sure has to be revised!

indicators.note: the letters must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: The Victorian novelist's work needs editing.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot (Mary Ann Evans) was a woman writer.

clue.text: Brightly coloured creature in a book apiarists read

indicators.note: the letters are inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A colourful animal appears in a book beekeepers read.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African animal with a rich chestnut coat and striped legs.

clue.text: Strike-breaker, in an extended period, makes mistakes

indicators.note: the strike-breaker is placed inside the period word

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
a rat is a worker who breaks a strike

explanation.surface: A scab working for a long time gets things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors, especially printing errors.

clue.text: Dismal half hour in the plant

parts.note: blue means sad, dismal
on ship a bell is struck each half hour of a watch

explanation.surface: A gloomy half hour spent in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: At sea, bells are rung every half hour of a watch, so a 'bell' marks a half hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell is a spring woodland flower.
